chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun from Abdullah ibn al-Rahman from Misma' Abu Sayyar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I dislike for my nation that a man goes to bed with his wife in the middle of the month or at the new moon, for the rebels of the devils and Jinn overwhelm the children of Adam, causing them to become possessed and insane. Have you not seen that the one afflicted by epilepsy is struck down in the middle of the month and at the new moon?'

key_terms.غُرَّةِ الْهِلالِ: the new moon / first day of the month

ai.seo_question: Why is marital intimacy disliked during the middle of the lunar month in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Sahl ibn Ziyad narrates from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) that the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) discouraged marital intimacy during the middle of the lunar month and on the first day (al-ghurrat), linking these times to heightened activity of 'Marada' (rebellious) Jinn. This tradition reflects the Shia cosmological view that spiritual vulnerabilities during specific lunar phases can manifest as physical ailments like epilepsy (al-musab), a concept deeply rooted in both hadith literature and classical tafsir.

en.sarwar: 5. Sahl ibn Ziyad has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hassan from Shammun from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman from Misma’ abu Sayyar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘I dislike for my followers that one of them goes to bed with his wife in the middle of the month or when it is new moon because the rebels of satans and Jinn overwhelm children of Adam; they become possessed by Jinn are and insane. You can see that those possessed become epileptic in the middle and in the beginning of the month’”
